title: The Ninth Bell of Brasswater
premise: In the tidal city of Brasswater, a municipal tide clock has lost its governor wheel hours before the storm gates must close. Captain Iris Vale and a divided salvage crew investigate from the docked airship Kestrel. Three competing institutions claim the missing wheel. The crew must establish who moved it, preserve evidence and keep ordinary life moving while a storm approaches. Travel takes time; messages and rumours do not move people or possessions. A name mentioned in conversation does not make its owner present.

passages.chapterTitle: The Letter on the Chart Table
passages.title: Three People and an Unopened Letter
paragraphs: Rain tapped the chart-room skylight. Iris set the damaged governor sketch between Tamsin and Ren. The engineer had come up from the engine room ten minutes earlier; the courier had been waiting beside the table. Beyond the closed door, a speaking tube carried the pilot’s request for a departure time. Iris left it unanswered.
“The notch is wrong,” Tamsin said, pointing to the pencil outline. “A wheel cut like that would bind before the third turn. Either the drawing is old, or someone has shown us the wrong part.”
Ren kept a sealed letter flat beneath his palm. “The registrar told me to deliver this directly. She did not tell me what it says.”

Iris recognised Mara Vale’s small, square handwriting on the envelope. Her sister was across the city at the Archive, not waiting somewhere aboard the ship. Iris could ask her about the drawing later. For now she had a sketch, a courier’s account and an unopened letter. She refused to treat any of them as proof of a theft.
“Keep the seal intact,” she said. “First, tell us exactly where you collected it.” Tamsin drew a clean sheet from the chart drawer and waited for his answer.

relationships.notes: Trusts her engineering judgement; disagrees about financial risk.
Respects the captain but wants authority to inspect the damaged mechanism.
Employs him as courier; has not heard the contents of his letter.
Wants to honour his delivery promise before answering questions.
Sisters who exchange occasional letters; Mara is not aboard.
Trusts her sister to keep written evidence intact.
Unrelated people sharing a surname; acquaintances through dock trade.
Estranged cousins; current intentions are not shared.
Worries that a public inquiry will implicate the family.
Siblings with separate jobs and separate possessions.
Professional colleagues who share medical updates when contacted.
Relies on her stock counts.
Registrar and vault keeper; formal chain of custody.
Communicate by roof signal; delivery can be delayed.
Overlapping authority; each requires separate signatures.
Coordinate departure and mooring safety.
Occasional paid market errands.
Friendly rivals; no automatic knowledge sharing.
Maintains the outdoor instruments she reads.
Carries island supplies only on scheduled crossings.

threads.notes: The map vault has an unaccounted sleeve.

canon.cargoNotes: Three sealed freight crates remain in the Kestrel hold. Shared operating funds are 684 crowns; personal money is not shared money.

narrationStyle: Close third person, past tense. Clear physical staging, distinct voices, restrained description and grounded causality.
artStyle: Painterly brass-and-timber maritime fantasy; overcast daylight.

preferences.writingGuide: Keep the scene focused on the people physically present. Mention background facts only when they affect an immediate action or decision.

sceneBrief.purpose: Compare the damaged governor sketch with the courier’s account without opening the sealed letter.
sceneBrief.tension: The crew must distinguish a witness report from a proven fact.
sceneBrief.stopAt: A decision about the next interview; nobody travels or opens the letter yet.

lore.title: Transit and communication
lore.text: The Kestrel is docked. City districts require travel. A radio or written message conveys only its stated content. Physical possessions remain with their recorded owner or container until an evidenced transfer.

lore.title: Archive custody
lore.text: Catalogue sleeves travel separately from original maps. A keeper signs every removal.

lore.title: Clinic routine
lore.text: Ordinary amber vials are counted every morning; they have no established connection to the missing mechanism.

lore.title: Unrevealed island lead
lore.text: A hidden planning possibility: the island shipment may connect the governor to an old flood inquiry. This is not established history. Hidden marker: violet albatross.

rules.text: Characters and objects do not teleport. Mentioning an absent person does not make them present or grant them knowledge.
